P1.evidence: Frame delivered in full and agreed: 'really just want to understand what's going on with your fitness right now, what challenges are you facing, and also just a clarity on what you're looking to accomplish. And then from there, if we can help with that, can jump into all the details about what we've got going on. Is good?' Open question immediately after: 'in your opinion, what would you say is the biggest challenge that you're having with your fitness right now?' P1a partial — the rep confirmed he had setter notes ('Well, I got some notes about you. Yeah. Just a little bit.') but never read anything back, so the prospect got no sense of being already known.

P2.evidence: Age asked ('How old are you right now? How young are you?') and weight asked, though not until 00:40:56 and after the price; height never captured. Current training captured properly — 'what have you been doing workout-wise over these recently, let's say the last few months?' produced splits, four to five days, assault bike, rower, walking. Injuries asked directly ('Have you had any injuries in your legs or anything?') but duration never pursued and the shoulder was left at 'pretty much healed'. Everything else missed: occupation was volunteered ('I'm a financial advisor, so I work a lot in an office') and never asked; no health-conditions question at any point in 48 minutes with a 61-year-old at 260 lb; diet never asked — the prospect volunteered 20 years of vegetarianism into the middle of the nutrition pitch; sleep raised only as something the programme does not track quantitatively, never as a question; energy never mentioned.

P3.evidence: The best phase on the call. Goal clarification was clean — 'when you say like all around, being in all around shape, that's just like moving better, having more endurance, looking better, dropping the weight. Is that what you mean?' The can't-do-it-now probe landed the Appalachian Trail and hiking with his wife. The why-now bridge worked twice: 'considering that you've never done that, we're here talking about potentially you working with Trevor and having a coach... why? It's a big change' produced the deepest line of the call, 'at some point you realize that you have more years behind you than you do in front of you and you can't waste any more time.' Reflect-back was accurate and confirmed. What did not run: 'who else does that impact' — the wife surfaced only as a training partner question ('do you think that you would be working out with your wife? Is she into this at all?'), never as the person paying the cost of his condition, which is exactly the thread that would have pre-empted the spouse objection an hour later.

P4.evidence: Asked cleanly whether he had ever worked with anyone ('have you ever worked with somebody like to keep you accountable and to teach you different types of workouts?') and got 'I've bought a program here and there... but it's all, here's the program, go for it.' Then never asked what happened with any of them — the single most useful unasked question on this call, since it is the direct proof that information without accountability fails for him. Root cause was drawn out well: 'what have you been procrastinating on around your fitness?' produced the office-day pattern and the six-week habit failure, and 'Any reason why not? Especially since you said accountability is one of your kind of biggest' produced 'it's too easy to talk yourself into saying, I know enough. I can do it myself.' The prospect named the gap himself in his own metaphor — 'I'm a good enough coach to get me this far, but I'm not a championship coach.'

P5.evidence: Never ran. The nearest attempt was a motivation question, not a consequence one: 'if there is something that you want to do in 10 years, what do you think like your motivation level would be to start really taking action towards it, like right now?' The prospect then supplied the entire consequence frame himself, unprompted and better than the script would have — 'I see old people who can't move, and I don't want to be one of them', 'I don't want to be the 70 year old who watches TV', 'I lost some time because of that and some cool stuff'. The rep acknowledged it and moved on. No 'is that something you're willing to settle for', no 'why not', no line in the sand. Per the scoring rule, volunteered information the rep never asked for is a miss.

P6.evidence: Both commitment moves eventually ran, but after the price and after the objection, which inverts the point of the phase. P6a arrived at 00:43:07 as 'as far as working with Trevor and the program, what you know about it now, do you feel it would work for you?' and got an unambiguous 'Oh yeah, I have no doubts on that score' — a yes that would have been worth ten times more banked before the number. P6b arrived as 'if she was here and she's like, Dan, go for it... Is there anything else that's coming up for you?' P6c is a clear miss: the prospect asked for the price at 00:29:00 ('hit me with the cost') and the rep gave it immediately with no commitment check and no consequence frame behind it.

P11.evidence: Never reachable — the prospect deferred to his wife and no agreement was reached, so there was no payment to collect, no Trevor call to book and no agreement to sign. The rep did describe the onboarding sequence accurately as a future state ('figure out the payment plan or process the investment... get you into the app, get you into the community, get you on a call with Trevor').

objection_plays.detail: Trigger was explicit and early: 'I'll talk it over with the wife, see what she says. You know, I can't just spend that kind of money without talking to her.' The rep let it sit for ten minutes and kept presenting, then ran two of the six moves. Ran: the belief check ('do you feel it would work for you?') and a variant of the obstacles question ('how do you plan on explaining it to her?'). Did not run: 'is there any reason she would NOT want you stronger and less in pain' — a gift on this call, since the wife is the person he keeps missing hikes with; 'is this genuinely needing her input or asking permission to bet on yourself'; and 'this isn't a joint decision like buying a house'. The rep actively backed away from the frame — 'I'm not trying to cause any friction. I'm the wife and stuff' — and instead handed the prospect a script to sell his wife on his behalf. The scripted fallback of a refundable deposit was never offered, and no follow-up call was booked despite the prospect volunteering he would speak to her 'within the next hour or two'.

'Just don't make any decisions right away. I got to think things.' Only the first move ran — the can-this-get-you-there belief check, answered with a flat yes. None of the rest: no 'what makes you feel it can', no 'so what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'when do you make a different decision'. The prospect had already handed the rep the perfect hook for that last one — 'you have more years behind you than you do in front of you and you can't waste any more time' — and it was never used against the stall.

Soft money trigger — 'It's just 9,000 bucks. I got to make sure it's in the budget' and 'it's not cheap, but I just got to fit it into my budget.' The rep did isolate ('Is there anything else that's coming up for you, maybe around the price or like anything else as far as like any possible hesitations?') and got a no, which is the correct first move. Nothing after it: no 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place', no invitation to an honest financial conversation, and none of the financial-picture questions. Most consequentially, the rep had already volunteered that plans and financing exist but never structured one live — the prospect left having to fit $9,000 into a budget without knowing what the monthly number would be.
Timing pressure ran in the programme's favour — the prospect argued urgency himself.
No fear or doubt about the programme working; he stated outright belief.

notes: Genuinely good discovery — the why-now probe at 61 was the best question anyone asked in this batch — and then the process collapsed at the transition. Price was handed over on request with no consequence frame and no commitment banked, so when the wife objection arrived the rep had nothing to hold him to and coached the prospect on how to sell his own spouse instead of running OB. The concrete coaching action is the exit: a prospect who believes fully, finds the price unsurprising and is speaking to his wife within two hours should leave with a booked follow-up time and a structured monthly figure, not an email address.
